hook.text: Silver killed bacteria in ancient Greece — nanosilver does it a thousand times more efficiently.

buildup.text: Silver nanoparticles release ions that pierce bacterial membranes and disrupt DNA.

discovery.text: Huge surface area delivers ions faster — micrograms of nanosilver can sterilize a liter of water.

twist.text: Nanosilver in wastewater may also kill beneficial bacteria in ecosystems and treatment plants.

climax.text: Regulators now limit nanosilver in consumer goods but allow it in wound dressings and water filters.

punchline.text: Silver shrunk to nano becomes a tiny germ killer.

quiz.question: How does nanosilver kill bacteria?
options: It heats up and burns bacterial cells
Silver ions from its large surface area damage membranes and DNA
It blocks light that bacteria need to survive
